questions.topic: Locus of mid-points of equal chords
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The locus of the mid-points of all equal chords in a circle is the circumference of the circle concentric with the given circle and having radius equal to the distance of equal chords from the center.
Reason (R): Locus of all points at a fixed distance from a fixed point is a circle with the fixed point as center and fixed distance as radius.

options.a: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
options.b: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
options.c: Assertion is true but Reason is false.
options.d: Assertion is false but Reason is true.

questions.solution: (a) Both true and R explains A. Equal chords are equidistant from the centre, so their mid-points (feet of perpendiculars from the centre) are all at that fixed distance from the centre; by R their locus is a concentric circle of that radius.

marking_points.point: Correct option (a): Both true and R explains A. Equal chords are equidistant from the centre, so their mid-points (feet of perpendiculars from the centre) are all at that fixed distance from the centre; by R their locus is a concentric circle of that radius.

questions.topic: Componendo and dividendo
questions.question:
Assertion (A): If x/3 = y/5, then (x + y)/(x − y) = 6.
Reason (R): If a/b = c/d, then (a + b)/(a − b) = (c + d)/(c − d).

options.b: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.

questions.topic: Comparing rates of return
questions.question:
Assertion (A): It is better to invest in 10%, ₹100 shares at ₹120 than in 8%, ₹100 shares at ₹72.
Reason (R): A rate of return (RoR) indicates how much an investment's value has changed over time relative to what it cost.

options.a: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
options.b: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
options.c: Assertion is true but Reason is false.
options.d: Assertion is false but Reason is true.

questions.solution: (d) Assertion is false but Reason is true. Return on first = 10 × 100/120 = 8.33%; on second = 8 × 100/72 = 11.11%; the second is the better investment, so A is false. R is a correct description of rate of return.

marking_points.point: Correct option (d): Assertion is false but Reason is true. Return on first = 10 × 100/120 = 8.33%; on second = 8 × 100/72 = 11.11%; the second is the better investment, so A is false. R is a correct description of rate of return.

questions.topic: Class marks to class intervals; histogram mode
questions.question:
The daily wages of workers in a construction unit were recorded as follows:
Class Marks (Wages): 425, 475, 525, 575, 625, 675
No. of workers: 6, 12, 15, 17, 7, 13
(a) Form a frequency distribution table with class intervals
(b) Find modal wage by plotting a histogram.
questions.solution: (a) Class width = 50, so intervals are class mark ± 25: 400–450 (6), 450–500 (12), 500–550 (15), 550–600 (17), 600–650 (7), 650–700 (13). (b) Draw the histogram (e.g. x-axis 2 cm = ₹50 with kink, y-axis 2 cm = 2 workers). Modal class 550–600; join the top corners of the tallest bar to the adjacent bars crosswise and drop a perpendicular from the intersection: mode ≈ ₹558 (by formula 550 + (17 − 15)/(34 − 15 − 7) × 50 = ₹558.33; key reads ₹557.50 from the graph).

questions.topic: Tangents from an external point
questions.question: Use ruler and compass only for answering this question. Draw a circle of radius 4 cm. Mark the centre as O. Mark a point P outside the circle at a distance of 7 cm from the centre. Construct two tangents to the circle from the external point P. Measure and write down the length of any one tangent.
questions.solution: Draw circle (O, 4 cm); mark P with OP = 7 cm. Bisect OP to get its mid-point M; with M as centre and MO as radius draw a circle cutting the given circle at Q and R. Join PQ and PR — these are the tangents. Length PQ = PR = √(7² − 4²) = √33 ≈ 5.7 cm (key measures 5.8 cm; 5.7–5.8 acceptable).

questions.topic: Central and inscribed angles; isosceles triangles with radii
concepts: angle at centre = twice angle at circumference
questions.question:
In the given figure, O is the centre of the circle. If ∠AOB = 140° and ∠OAC = 50°; find :
(a) ∠ACB,
(b) ∠OBC,
(c) ∠OAB,
(d) ∠CBA.
questions.solution: (a) C lies on the minor arc AB, so ∠ACB = ½ reflex ∠AOB = ½(360° − 140°) = 110°. (b) In quadrilateral OACB: ∠OBC = 360° − (140° + 110° + 50°) = 60°. (c) OA = OB (radii) ⇒ ∠OAB = ∠OBA = (180° − 140°)/2 = 20°. (d) ∠CBA = ∠OBC − ∠OBA = 60° − 20° = 40°.
questions.figure_desc: Circle with centre O on the left of chord AB (B at top, A at bottom), C on the circle to the right of AB; OA, OB, AC, BC drawn; ∠AOB = 140° at O and ∠OAC = 50° at A.

questions.topic: Similar triangles with a common angle; area ratio
questions.question:
In ΔABC, ∠ABC = ∠DAC, AB = 8 cm, AC = 4 cm, AD = 5 cm. (D is a point on BC, joined to A.)
(a) Prove that ΔACD is similar to Δ BCA.
(b) Find BC and CD.
(c) Find area of ΔACD : area of ΔABC.
questions.solution: (a) In ΔACD and ΔBCA: ∠ACD = ∠BCA (common), ∠DAC = ∠ABC (given) ⇒ ΔACD ~ ΔBCA (AA). So AC/BC = CD/CA = AD/BA. (b) 4/BC = 5/8 ⇒ BC = 6.4 cm. CD/4 = 5/8 ⇒ CD = 2.5 cm. (c) ar(ΔACD)/ar(ΔBCA) = (AD/AB)² = (5/8)² = 25/64, i.e. 25 : 64.

questions.topic: First term and ratio from sums of term blocks
questions.question: Sheena noticed that the sum of the first three terms of a G.P. is 16 and the sum of next three terms is 128. Find the first term and common ratio of the G.P.
questions.solution: a + ar + ar² = 16 and ar³ + ar⁴ + ar⁵ = r³(a + ar + ar²) = 128. Dividing: r³ = 128/16 = 8 ⇒ r = 2. Then a(1 + 2 + 4) = 16 ⇒ a = 16/7. First term 16/7, common ratio 2.

marking_points.point: Sum of first three terms equation
Sum of next three terms = r³ × first sum

questions.topic: Reflections in y-axis and a horizontal line; identifying a square
questions.question:
Use a graph sheet for this question.
(a) Plot A(0, 3), B(2, 1) and C(4, −1).
(b) Reflect points B and C in the y-axis and name their images as B' and C' respectively. Plot and write coordinates of the points B' and C'.
(c) Reflect point A in the line BB' and name its images as A'.
(d) Plot and write coordinates of point A'.
(e) Join the points ABA'B' and give the geometrical name of the closed figure so formed.
questions.solution: (a) Plot A(0, 3), B(2, 1), C(4, −1) with scale 2 cm = 1 unit. (b) Reflection in y-axis: (x, y) → (−x, y): B'(−2, 1), C'(−4, −1). (c)/(d) BB' is the line y = 1; reflecting A(0, 3) in y = 1 gives A'(0, −1). (e) ABA'B': diagonals AA' (x = 0, length 4) and BB' (y = 1, length 4) are equal, perpendicular and bisect each other at (0, 1), so ABA'B' is a square.

questions.topic: Checking proportion from a table; missing values
questions.question:
The profit in rupees in a local chat centre 'MANTRA CHATS' and the number of customers who visited the chat centre are tabulated below for each week for one month.
Week: Week 1, Week 2, Week 3, Week 4
Number of customers: 1400, 5600, x, 3212
Profit in ₹: 28000, 112000, 32140, y
Find:
(a) if the number of customers and profit per week is in continued proportion or not? Justify your answer
(b) the value of x and y.
questions.solution: (a) 1400/28000 = 1/20 and 5600/112000 = 1/20. The ratio customers : profit is the same (1 : 20) each week, so the number of customers and profit are in (direct) proportion. (b) x/32140 = 1/20 ⇒ x = 1607; 3212/y = 1/20 ⇒ y = ₹64,240.

questions.topic: Scale factor: length, area and volume
questions.question:
A model of a ship is made to a scale of 1 : 250. Calculate :
(a) the length of the ship, if the length of the model is 1.6 m.
(b) the area of the deck of the ship in km², if the area of the deck of the model is 2.4 m².
(c) the volume of the model, if the volume of the ship is 1 km³.
questions.solution: k = 1/250. (a) Length of ship = 1.6 × 250 = 400 m. (b) Area of ship = 2.4 × 250² = 150000 m² = 0.15 km². (c) Volume of model = 1 km³ × (1/250)³ = 10⁹ m³ / 15625000 = 64 m³.

questions.topic: Compound inequation with number line
questions.question: Solve the following inequation and write the solution set: 13x − 5 < 15x + 4 < 7x + 12, x ∈ R. Represent the solution on a real number line.
questions.solution: 13x − 5 < 15x + 4 ⇒ −9 < 2x ⇒ x > −4½. 15x + 4 < 7x + 12 ⇒ 8x < 8 ⇒ x < 1. Solution set {x : −4½ < x < 1, x ∈ R}. Number line: open circles at −4½ and 1 with the segment between shaded.

questions.topic: Missing frequency from mean; median from ogive
questions.question:
A life insurance agent found the following data of age distribution of 100 policy holders, where f is an unknown frequency.
Age in years: 15-20, 20-25, 25-30, 30-35, 35-40, 40-45, 45-50, 50-55
No. of Policy Holders: 7, 12, 15, 22, f, 14, 8, 4
(a) If the mean age of the policy holders is 35.65 years, find the unknown frequency f.
(b) Use a graph paper to find the median and median class of the distribution.
questions.solution: (a) Class marks 17.5 … 52.5; take A = 37.5, d = x − A: d = −20, −15, −10, −5, 0, 5, 10, 15; fd = −140, −180, −150, −110, 0, 70, 80, 60; Σfd = −370, Σf = 82 + f. Mean = 37.5 − 370/(82 + f) = 35.65 ⇒ 370/(82 + f) = 1.85 ⇒ 82 + f = 200 ⇒ f = 118. (b) c.f.: 7, 19, 34, 56, 174, 188, 196, 200. Plot the ogive (upper limits vs c.f., starting (15, 0)). N = 200, median = 100th term: reading across from 100 gives median ≈ 37 years (by interpolation 35 + (100 − 56)/118 × 5 ≈ 36.9; the key's freehand curve reads 38). Median class 35–40. Note: the stated total of 100 policy holders is inconsistent with the mean 35.65 — f = 18 would make 100 but give mean 33.8; the mean condition gives f = 118 (N = 200), as used by the key.

questions.topic: Two squares: sum of areas and difference of perimeters
questions.question: The sum of the areas of two squares is 468 m². If the difference of their perimeters is 24 m, find the sides of the two squares.
questions.solution: Let sides be x and y (x > y). 4x − 4y = 24 ⇒ y = x − 6. x² + (x − 6)² = 468 ⇒ 2x² − 12x − 432 = 0 ⇒ x² − 6x − 216 = 0 ⇒ (x − 18)(x + 12) = 0 ⇒ x = 18 (reject −12). y = 12. Sides 18 m and 12 m.

questions.topic: Identity using a² − b² factorisation
questions.question: Prove that: (sin⁴θ − cos⁴θ + 1) cosec²θ = 2.
questions.solution: LHS = [(sin²θ + cos²θ)(sin²θ − cos²θ) + 1] cosec²θ = [sin²θ − cos²θ + 1] cosec²θ = [sin²θ − (1 − sin²θ) + 1] cosec²θ = 2sin²θ × 1/sin²θ = 2 = RHS.

questions.topic: Difference of 4th terms of APs with same d
questions.question: Two A.P.'s have the same common difference. The first term for one of these is −1, and that for the other is −8. Find the difference for the 4th term of the two A.P.'s?
questions.solution: Let common difference be d. T₄ of first AP = −1 + 3d; T₄ of second AP = −8 + 3d. Difference = (−1 + 3d) − (−8 + 3d) = 7 (the second AP's 4th term is 7 less, i.e. −7 taking second minus first).

questions.topic: Total surface area of a cylinder cut along its height
questions.question: A solid metallic cylinder is cut into two identical halves along its height. The diameter of the cylinder is 7 cm and the height is 10 cm. Find : (a) The total surface area (both the halves). (b) The total cost of painting the two halves at the rate of ₹30 per cm². (use π = 22/7)
questions.solution: r = 3.5 cm, h = 10 cm. Cutting along the height adds two rectangular faces of 10 cm × 7 cm. (a) TSA of both halves = TSA of cylinder + 2 × rectangle = 2πr(r + h) + 2(10 × 7) = 2 × (22/7) × 3.5 × 13.5 + 140 = 297 + 140 = 437 cm². (b) Cost = 437 × 30 = ₹13,110.

questions.topic: Selling price including GST at distributor stage
questions.question: A shopkeeper bought a TV from a distributor at a discount of 25% on the listed price of ₹32000. The shopkeeper sells the TV to a consumer at the listed price. If the sales are intra-state and the rate of GST is 18%, What is the selling price of the TV including tax (under GST) by the distributor?
questions.solution: Distributor's selling price = 32000 − 25% of 32000 = ₹24000. GST = 18% of 24000 = ₹4320 (CGST ₹2160 + SGST ₹2160). Price including tax = 24000 + 4320 = ₹28,320.

questions.topic: Speed of boat from changing angle of depression
questions.question: A man is watching from the top of a tower, a boat speeding away from the tower. The angle of depression from the top of the tower to the boat is 60° when the boat is 80 m from the tower. After 10 seconds, the angle of depression becomes 30°. What is the speed of the boat? (Assume that the boat is running in still water).
questions.solution: Let AB be the tower, C the first position (BC = 80 m), D the position after 10 s. tan 60° = AB/80 ⇒ AB = 80√3 m. tan 30° = AB/BD ⇒ BD = 80√3 × √3 = 240 m. CD = 240 − 80 = 160 m. Speed = 160/10 = 16 m/s (= 57.6 km/h).
